item.title: Mamdani Says Child Was in Car When ICE Agent Shot New York Man
item.description: A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent shot and wounded a man in New York City on Thursday, prompting Mayor Zohran Mamdani to demand an end to ICE operations in the city.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent shot and wounded a man in New York City on Thursday, prompting Mayor Zohran Mamdani to demand an end to ICE operations in the city.Mamdani said early reports indicated agents surrounded the man before firing multiple rounds in the residential neighborhood of Marble Hill in the Bronx. A five-year-old child was in the man’s vehicle, Mamdani said, adding officials believed the child was physically unharmed.The shooting occurred at about 4 p.m., the New York Police Department said. The man was conscious and receiving treatment at a nearby hospital.“This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation,” Mamdani said in a statement. “I have called the President; when we speak I will demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city.”The man had been sought by ICE as part of a federal operation and had prior criminal convictions, according to a person familiar with the matter, who also confirmed ICE’s involvement in the shooting. It wasn’t immediately clear what led to the incident. The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, didn’t respond to a request for comment.A series of shootings involving federal immigration agents, including incidents earlier this year when US citizens were killed, has drawn national attention to the Trump administration’s enforcement efforts.New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she had been briefed on the shooting and called on federal authorities to explain what happened.“We expect federal authorities to provide a full and transparent accounting of the circumstances surrounding this incident,” she wrote in a post on X. “New Yorkers deserve to know exactly what happened and why.”The NYPD said it wasn’t involved in the incident and had no officers at the scene when the shooting occurred. The city’s sanctuary policies generally limit local cooperation with federal immigration authorities. Mamdani called for ICE to leave the city’s neighborhoods, hospitals, streets and children, saying he would not stand by while agents “terrorize our communities.”--With assistance from Alicia A. Caldwell.(Updates with Mamdani comments throughout.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Malaysia PM Calls Prabowo Over Haze as Kuala Lumpur Chokes
item.description: Malaysia’s prime minister has contacted Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto about efforts to tackle the thick smog that has choked Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country as weeks of devastating wildfires consume swathes of the neighboring archipelago.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- Malaysia’s prime minister has contacted Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto about efforts to tackle the thick smog that has choked Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country as weeks of devastating wildfires consume swathes of the neighboring archipelago.Air quality in the capital was in the “very unhealthy” range as of Thursday afternoon, according to data from IQAir, and ranked as the most polluted city in the world. Menara Merdeka Maybank, the world’s second-tallest building, and the iconic Petronas Twin Towers were faint silhouettes, barely visible behind the haze.Johor, a state at the tip of Malaysian peninsula, closed schools through the end of the week, affecting about 617,000 students, according to the state education ministry. “The haze situation is indeed worrying,” Anwar Ibrahim told reporters, according to state-owned news agency Bernama. He said Prabowo had “agreed to take the necessary steps,” without providing detail. Indonesia’s Government Communication Agency referred queries to the foreign ministry, which did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Parts of Southeast Asia have been blanketed in thick fumes for over a month as Indonesia endures one of its worst wildfire seasons in years. The blazes are linked to the long-running use of slash-and-burn farming practices, exacerbated by a powerful El Niño that has brought dry conditions to the region.Malaysia is seeking expedited talks with Indonesia to send a team to help extinguish the fires. Anwar said the government was also seeking to arrange a meeting of regional environment ministers, though it had already taken steps to reduce the impact at home, including increasing cloud seeding.Johor Chief Minister Onn Hafiz Ghazi, at the helm of one of the most affected regions, has also called for an emergency meeting of regional leaders, saying the Association of Southeast Asian Nations “needs to play a more active role and hold an emergency meeting to address this crisis collectively,” he wrote in a Facebook post.At least five flights were disrupted at Senai International Airport in Johor early Thursday as haze reduced visibility below aviation safety requirements, the Malay Mail reported. Several aircraft were diverted to Kuala Lumpur and Singapore while other departures were delayed at their points of origin.Last week, organizers of the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon canceled a kids’ race over health concerns while pressing on with other categories, including the full and half marathons.Greenpeace Malaysia and several civil-society groups held a demonstration Wednesday calling for legislation that would give authorities clearer powers to investigate, obtain evidence and take enforcement action against companies linked to transboundary environmental damage.The green group said stronger domestic laws “cannot address every regional challenge on its own” and would need to be complemented by mechanisms and bilateral channels from Asean, which includes Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines, to obtain evidence about fires.“Public anger on haze needs to bring about a twofold response: holding to account those who are culpable while recognizing and supporting those who are doing their utmost to protect the forests and farmlands at risk,” said Joseph D’Cruz, the chief executive officer of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil. --With assistance from Ben Otto, Rieka Rahadiana, Megan Durisin, Ramsey Al-Rikabi and Netty Ismail.(Updates with details from Malaysia’s prime minister from first paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: UK Police Arrest Latvian Men Found at Second Airbase Used by US
item.description: British police arrested two men on suspicion of trespassing and national security offenses at an airbase that’s used by the US for intelligence and analysis work, just weeks after a suspected terror plot at another base that was home to American bombers.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- British police arrested two men on suspicion of trespassing and national security offenses at an airbase that’s used by the US for intelligence and analysis work, just weeks after a suspected terror plot at another base that was home to American bombers.The two men, both Latvian nationals in their 30s, were arrested late Wednesday following security patrols near RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire. Officers found a “small breach” of the perimeter fence, counterterror police said in a statement. There was nothing to suggest at this stage that the two separate airbase incidents were related, police said, adding that their investigation was at an early stage and that they were keeping an open mind about the motive.RAF Molesworth, located about 90 miles (145 kilometers) north of London, houses the US Joint Intelligence Operations Center Europe and is garrisoned by a US Air Force group.The incursion will deepen scrutiny of the security at airbases in Britain that are used by US forces, as the UK warns of an escalation in sabotage plots involving so-called proxies directed by Iran and Russia.The Pentagon evacuated its bombers at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire last week after five men were found near the base along with three vans and a quantity of fuel. Several other arrests have since been made and the probe is ongoing. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said it was likely that Iran was involved in the incident.President Donald Trump’s decision to move the bombers may embolden Iran and Russia’s use of proxies to carry out sabotage attacks, current and former British officials told Bloomberg. The UK is concerned that hostile states will take confidence that they can force changes to Western defense arrangements and destabilize their enemies for the relatively small cost of hiring local criminal proxies, the people said.Richard Knighton, the head of Britain’s armed forces, said on Thursday that the country’s bases were safe. “We take the security of all of our bases in Europe enormously seriously,” he said, calling the US move an “operational decision.” Knighton added that the UK has “enormously close relationships from an intelligence perspective and operationally with the US, and that’s what gives me confidence around the safety and security of our bases here.”--With assistance from Sachin Ravikumar.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.
